reviews.body: Verified the tests-only reconciliation at eef13f46824466eefb86fbdf483ea27b810a2309. Main’s production implementation and existing reproduction/CTE coverage are preserved; the three additional cases cover dollar-free SQL comment markers inside strings, bracketed identifiers and block comments. The complete native Power BI topology module passed: 63 tests, no failures or skips.

review_comments.body: 💡 Edge Case: -- inside a / / block comment strips the closing */ The new regex only skips single-quoted literals. For a T-SQL query such as `SELECT a#(lf)/* old filter -- removed */#(lf)FROM orders`, it treats the `--` inside the block comment as a line comment and deletes everything up to the newline, including the `*/`. Once the whitespace is collapsed, the block comment never closes, so it covers the rest of the query: `orders` disappears and no lineage is produced, with nothing logged. Before this change the flattened query still had a valid `/* ... */` and parsed correctly, so this is a regression for queries that put `--` inside block comments. A fix is to match block comments in the same pass and keep them unchanged (or remove them) before handling `--`, and to add a test for this case. **Match string literals and block comments before `--` so that neither gets cut:** ```` cleaned_sql = re.sub( r"('(?:[^']|'')*')|(/\*.*?\*/)|--[^ ]*", lambda match: match.group(1) or match.group(2) or "", cleaned_sql, flags=re.DOTALL, ) ```` ✅ Fixed by `@pcbeingused333` in 8a86891 Reply for a change | Was this helpful? React with 👍 / 👎

This regex treats `--` inside quoted identifiers and block comments as a line comment. For example, `SELECT [a--b] FROM dbo.orders` becomes `SELECT [a` and returns no tables, while the baseline finds `orders`. Likewise, `SELECT * FROM dbo.orders /* -- audit */ JOIN dbo.customers ON 1=1` loses `customers` because the closing `*/` is removed. Please preserve decoded newlines and let the T-SQL parser handle comments, or use complete lexical handling, and add regressions for both cases.

This assertion still passes if `--` is mistakenly stripped from inside `'a--b'`: the parser still finds `orders` before the damaged literal. Please also assert that the returned SQL retains `'a--b'`, or put the literal before `FROM orders` so truncating it removes a required table reference. That would make the test catch the behavior its name promises.
